cards.text: The war with Benjamin is over, friend. Israel burned the Benjamite cities, and only 600 Benjamite men got away, hiding out at the rock of Rimmon. And back at Mizpah, the men of Israel had sworn an oath about Benjamin.

cards.question: What did the men of Israel swear back at Mizpah?

answers.text: Not one of us will give his daughter to a Benjamite
Not one of us will set foot on Benjamite land
Not one of us will ever trade with a Benjamite

cards.text: So the people come to Bethel and sit before God until evening, lifting up their voices and weeping bitterly. They won, and NOBODY is celebrating.

cards.question: Weeping before God at Bethel, what do the people cry out to the LORD?

answers.text: Asking why one tribe is missing from Israel
Asking why the battle took three whole days
Asking why Benjamin refused to hand anyone over

cards.text: Next day they're up early, building an altar and presenting burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then a question goes around: who among all the tribes didn't come to the assembly before the LORD?

cards.question: Israel had taken a solemn oath about anyone who failed to come up before the LORD at Mizpah. That person would surely face ___.

cards.text: Here's the turn, friend: the Israelites grieve for their brothers, the Benjamites. They say, “Today a tribe is cut off from Israel.”

cards.question: The Israelites ask what to do about wives for the Benjamite survivors. True or false: they're free to give the survivors their own daughters.

cards.text: Ever had your own promise box you in? That's Israel right now, so they turn to their other oath, ask which tribe failed to come up to Mizpah, and count the people.

cards.question: When the people are counted, which town had nobody at the assembly?

cards.text: This is where the story gets hard, friend, and I'm not going to soften it. The congregation sends 12,000 of their most valiant men to Jabesh-gilead.

cards.question: True or false: the congregation commands the men to put the people of Jabesh-gilead to the sword, including women and children.

cards.text: Every male, and every woman who has had relations with a man, is to be devoted to destruction. The young women who have not had relations with a man are the only ones left alive.

cards.question: The men find ___ young women in Jabesh-gilead and bring them to the camp at Shiloh.

cards.text: Then the whole congregation sends a message of peace to the Benjamites hiding at the rock of Rimmon.

cards.question: The Benjamites come back and are given the 400 women from Jabesh-gilead. Remember, 600 Benjamite men survived. So how does it work out?

answers.text: There are not enough women for all of them
Every single survivor ends up with a wife
Some of the women go back to Jabesh-gilead

cards.text: The Benjamite survivors are still short of wives, and the people grieve for Benjamin, because the LORD had made a void in the tribes of Israel. So the elders ask it again: what do we do about wives for the ones who remain, since the women of Benjamin have been destroyed?

cards.question: The elders say there must be ___ for the survivors of Benjamin, so that a tribe of Israel won't be wiped out.

cards.text: But the oath still stands, because the Israelites had sworn, “Cursed is he who gives a wife to a Benjamite.” They are STUCK, friend.
Then the elders say, “But look,” and start giving directions: north of Bethel, east of the road up to Shechem, south of Lebonah. Friend, that's not directions, that's a dropped pin.

cards.question: What happens every year at that spot north of Bethel?

answers.text: A feast to the LORD in Shiloh
A gathering of the elders at Mizpah
A market for traders from every tribe

cards.text: So the elders give the Benjamites a command: “Go, hide in the vineyards”

cards.question: Hiding in the vineyards near Shiloh, what are the Benjamites told to watch for?

answers.text: The daughters of Shiloh coming out to dance
The priests of Shiloh coming out to pray
The fathers of Shiloh heading out to the road

cards.question: True or false: when the dancers come out, each Benjamite is to catch a wife from the daughters of Shiloh and then settle down in Shiloh.

cards.text: The elders even have a speech ready for the fathers or brothers who come to complain. They'll ask them to do Israel a favor by helping the Benjamites.

cards.question: The elders' loophole: since the fathers didn't actually ___ their daughters to the Benjamites, they have no guilt.

cards.text: And the Benjamites do exactly as instructed. They carry away the number of women they need from the dancers they catch.

cards.question: True or false: the Benjamites go back to their own inheritance, rebuild their cities and settle in them.

cards.text: Then everybody heads home, each to his own tribe, clan and inheritance. And the book of Judges ends with one sentence that sums up those days: there was no king in Israel.

cards.question: No king in Israel in those days. So what did everyone do?

answers.text: What was right in his own eyes
What was good in the sight of the LORD
What was written in the law of Moses

findings.problem: The card packs several beats into one long sentence: the promise-box joke, Israel turning to their other oath, the question about which tribe failed to come up, and the count of the people. Split it, or move the count to the choice card's setup.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The setup says "This is where the story gets hard, friend, and I'm not going to soften it" right before the true/false card asks whether the men were commanded to put the town to the sword, including women and children. The line tells the baker the answer is True, so it rules out False.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card opens by restating what stop 1, card 16 just answered ("still short of wives"). It then carries three beats: the shortage, the people's grief with its stated reason, and the elders' question. Drop the recap and keep the card to the grief and the elders' question.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: "do exactly as instructed" adds "exactly". The text only says "The Benjamites did as instructed" (Judges 21:23).

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The "dropped pin" joke sets up the elders' plan for the Benjamites to hide and carry off the dancing daughters of Shiloh. The joke is aimed at the directions, not at anyone in the story, so no reverence rule clearly forbids it. But it puts a laugh right at the setup of the women being carried away, in a passage that also includes the killing at Jabesh-gilead.
findings.question: In passages with killing or violence against women, should Papa Dorin hold back jokes around those moments, even jokes about a neutral detail like directions? Or is this joke acceptable?

findings.problem: The choice card asks about the line "everyone did what was right in his own eyes". The same line already appears in Judges 17:6, which is likely in an earlier lesson. The refrain rule says to ask about a repeated line only the first time it appears, but it doesn't say whether that means within this passage or across the book.
findings.question: Does the rule "When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears" apply only within one passage, or across passages (here Judges 17:6 and 21:25)?
